meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'again', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: It's another trick.
Rain again.

examples.text: Нина, не слушай. Это опять обман.
examples.trans: Nina, don't listen. It's another trick.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.
And does the governor support you?

examples.text: Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Prefix 'пере-' denotes crossing over, repeating, or exceeding a limit (stem 'держивать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to overcook, keep too long'.

examples.text: Опять вы передерживаете овощи, Максим Леонидович.
examples.trans: You are overcooking the vegetables again, Maxim Leonidovich.

examples.text: На кухне никто не хочет передерживать без причины.
examples.trans: In the kitchen nobody wants to overcook without a reason.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'vegetable' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Fresh vegetables are very healthy.

examples.text: Там мне дают только чистить овощи.
examples.trans: There they only give me vegetables to peel.
Chop fresh vegetables for the salad.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, that; it is', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: That's mine.
And this is for you.
And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'certainly', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Поймите, была маленькая ошибка. Вы уж нас извините.
examples.trans: Understand, there was a small mistake. Please forgive us.
Indeed, not very well at all.
Certainly much better than you!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.

examples.trans: I have a toy car.
Childhood was hard.
You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Chef, I didn't take it.
I don't know.
There wasn't enough money.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'al (in al dente)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Это уж будет не аль денте.
examples.trans: That will not be al dente anymore.
That is what is called al dente.

денте.gloss: dente (al dente, firm to the bite)

meanings.en: dente (al dente, firm to the bite)
meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'dente (al dente, firm to the bite)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Это уж будет не аль денте.
examples.trans: That will not be al dente anymore.
That is what is called al dente.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: May I have a look?
Can you smoke here?
Can I go and have a look?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Chef, I didn't take it.
I don't know.
I'm doing my homework.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'after', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Он за мной после концерта ухаживал.
examples.trans: He courted me after a concert once.
Let's talk after work.

examples.text: Он за мной после концерта ухаживал. В Москву звал замуж!
examples.trans: He courted me after a concert once. He asked me to marry him and come to Moscow!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: That's what you said.
That house is old.
Well, the thing you said.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'how; as', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: How was it in Hungary?
As you all know...
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to pour off, leak, dump'.

related.gloss: not to to pour off (negated infinitive)

examples.text: После того, как вы слили воду.
examples.trans: Right after you drain the boiling water.

examples.text: Хотя, если ему надо, пусть берет.
examples.trans: Although if he needs it, let him use it.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'water' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: There's water everywhere!
Give me some water.
Vanya, the water! There's water everywhere!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'over, above; at', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: The lamp is above the table.
Don't laugh at me.

examples.text: За поведение? Вы смеётесь надо мной?
examples.trans: For my conduct? Are you laughing at me?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to lower, put down'.

examples.text: Надо опустить овощи в воду со льдом.
examples.trans: You have to plunge the vegetables into ice water.

examples.text: На кухне никто не хочет опустить без причины.
examples.trans: In the kitchen nobody wants to lower without a reason.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in, into', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: How is it in Hungary?
I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'with', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Share with everyone.
I'm with Dad.
Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'ice' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Мы посидим на льду и половим рыбу.
examples.trans: We will sit on the ice and catch fish.
In winter the river became covered with thick ice.

examples.text: Нужно класть в стакан больше льда.
examples.trans: You need to put more ice into the glass.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.
Dad and Mum.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'зываться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be called'.

examples.trans: What's this town called?
The operation is called Golden Yard.

examples.text: Товарищ генерал, операция называется Золотой ярд.
examples.trans: Comrade General, the operation is called Golden Yard.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: What's this?
Look what I've got.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.
examples.trans: Hi! Look what I've got.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'translation, transfer' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Что в переводе с итальянского означает...
examples.trans: Which translated from Italian means...

examples.text: На нашей кухне уже есть новый перевод.
examples.trans: In our kitchen there is already a new translation.

meanings.note: Relational adjective formed with the Slavic suffix '-ский' ('pertaining to'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('Italian').

examples.trans: They called from the Italian restaurant.
We love Italian food.

examples.text: Кстати, звонили из итальянского ресторана. Дарят папе романтический ужин на двоих.
examples.trans: By the way, they called from the Italian restaurant. They're giving Dad a romantic dinner for two.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to mean, signify'.

examples.text: Что в переводе с итальянского означает...
examples.trans: Which translated from Italian means...

examples.text: На кухне никто не хочет означать без причины.
examples.trans: In the kitchen nobody wants to mean without a reason.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to feel', paired with 'почувствовать'.

examples.trans: I feel well.
Can you smell that?

examples.text: А с Пашей я снова чувствую себя женщиной.
examples.trans: And with Pasha I feel like a woman again.

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'плохо'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Well then, not bad.
He speaks Russian pretty well.

examples.text: Ну что же, неплохо. Ты молодец.
examples.trans: Well then, not bad. Good job.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'never', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я никогда не был на море.
examples.trans: I've never been to the sea.
No! Never!

examples.text: Я своему ребёнку никогда не вру.
examples.trans: I never lie to my child.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'would', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.

examples.text: Юле бы дублёнку купили, Славику бы ноутбук.
examples.trans: We could have bought Yulia a sheepskin coat, and Slavik a laptop.
Look who's talking.

подумать.gloss: to think (for a while), to think it over

meanings.en: to think (for a while), to think it over
meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'умать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to think (for a while), to think it over', paired with 'думать'.

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.
I've been thinking.
Think again.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to know'.

examples.trans: I don't know.
As you all know...

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'without', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: That's no problem.
This time there's no trick.
That's no problem at all.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'offense, resentment, hurt' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I will not forget this insult.
She was left with bitter resentment.

examples.text: Я всё равно не забуду эту обиду.
examples.trans: I will not forget this insult anyway.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'what; what a', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: What is your town like?
What a beautiful house!

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'there', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Everything's fine there.
Who's there?
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'at, by; (у меня) I have', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I have a toy car.
He's at our place.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.
examples.trans: Hi! Look what I've got.

meanings.note: Derived noun with agent/object suffix '-ник'/'-щик'/'-чик'. Common masculine noun meaning 'fridge' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The milk is in the fridge.
Whose fridge is this?

examples.text: Курица? Нет. А чей это холодильник?
examples.trans: Chicken? No. And whose fridge is this?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to see', paired with 'увидеть'.

examples.trans: I can see the toy car.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.
See the markers? They're from Japan!
